# abs

> Compute the [absolute value][absolute-value] of a double-precision floating-point number.

<section class="intro">

The [absolute value][absolute-value] is defined as

<!-- <equation class="equation" label="eq:absolute_value" align="center" raw="|x|" alt="Absolute value"> -->

```math
|x| = \begin{cases} x & \textrm{if}\ x \geq 0 \\ -x & \textrm{if}\ x < 0\end{cases}
```

<!-- </equation> -->

</section>

<!-- /.intro -->

<section class="usage">

## Usage

```javascript
var abs = require( '@stdlib/math/base/special/abs' );
```

#### abs( x )

Computes the [absolute value][absolute-value] of a double-precision floating-point number.

<!-- run: throws: false, timeout: 1000 -->

```javascript
var v = abs( -1.0 );
// returns 1.0
```

</section>

<!-- /.usage -->

<section class="examples">

## Examples

<!-- eslint no-undef: "error" -->

```javascript
var abs = require( '@stdlib/math/base/special/abs' );

console.log( abs( -3.14 ) );
```

</section>

<!-- /.examples -->

<section class="c">

## C APIs

<section class="usage">

### Usage

```c
#include "stdlib/math/base/special/abs.h"
```

#### stdlib_base_abs( x )

```c
double y = stdlib_base_abs( -5.0 );
```

</section>

<!-- /.usage -->

</section>

<!-- /.c -->
